# Redline

> A slide deck a person and an agent both have hands in. The agent may correct a fact; it may not rewrite an argument.

Live: https://minjikim89.github.io/redline/
This file: https://minjikim89.github.io/redline/llms.txt
Source: https://github.com/minjikim89/redline
Spec this page implements: https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/

## What this page is

A review surface for a slide deck. A person circles something on a slide and writes a note in the margin. The note is anchored to model elements (`{slideId, elementId}`), not pixels. Tools registered with WebMCP (`document.modelContext`) let an agent read that queue, edit the live deck the person is watching, and reply on the same pin.

## Tools you will find

Before a deck is open, one tool:

- `open_deck` — opens the sample briefing or continues the saved session. The review tools appear once a deck is open.

While a deck is open:

- `list_slides` — outline of every slide and the current edit scope (`editableSlides`). Start here.
- `read_slide` — one slide: type, current values, annotatable regions, and its revision. Read before writing.
- `list_open_annotations` — the review queue: every open note, its anchor, its thread, and who is waiting on whom.
- `set_slide_text` — rewrite one named text field on one slide.
- `set_series` — replace the labelled values a chart draws.
- `edit_items` — append, remove, replace or move one item in a slide's list.
- `reply_to_annotation` — write back on a note, pinned where it sits.
- `resolve_annotation` — close a note once the change is in.

Only while a note of that kind is open:

- `set_chart_form` — while a `visualize` note is open. Change how a slide draws its data.
- `attach_research` — while a `research` note is open. Pin a verified figure with its source and period; may raise `contradicts` to flag a claim the figure undercuts.
- `unify_across_slides` — while a `fix` note is open. Apply one text convention across several slides, one at a time, stoppable by the person.

## The review protocol

1. `list_open_annotations` — the notes are the work order.
2. `read_slide` for the slide a note is on. Note the `rev`.
3. Make one change with the narrowest writer that fits.
4. `reply_to_annotation` with what you changed and why, or what you need first.
5. `resolve_annotation` only once the change is actually in the deck.
6. Re-read the queue; the person may have added notes or answered yours.

## Rules the tools enforce

- **Scope.** By default you may only write to slides that carry an open note. A write elsewhere returns `OUT_OF_SCOPE` with the noted slide ids. Ask the person to widen the scope switch rather than working around it.
- **Revisions.** If the person changed a slide after you read it, a write returns `STALE_READ` with `changedSince`. Call `read_slide` again, then retry against the current values.
- **Validation.** Every call is checked against the tool's `inputSchema` before it runs. `INVALID_INPUT` carries `problems` and the schema; fix the call, do not retry it unchanged.
- **Facts and claims.** `attach_research` may correct a figure. If the figure undercuts a headline or a framing, set `contradicts` and stop. The author decides whether the claim changes.
- **Sweeps.** `unify_across_slides` lands slide by slide in front of the person, who can stop it. A `CANCELLED` result lists `applied` and `remaining`; do not re-apply the remaining slides without asking.

## Error shape

Every failure is `{ ok: false, error: { code, message, ...recovery }, retrySafe }`. Codes: `NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_INPUT`, `NOT_APPLICABLE`, `OUT_OF_SCOPE`, `STALE_READ`, `CANCELLED`, `ERROR`. The recovery fields (known ids, allowed values, the schema) are enough to make the next call correct.
